reason: The Commission confirms the Government adopted the strategy and a costed action plan on 21 January 2025. The only statement that it is applied is one line in a 2026 regulator report, with no measure named, and the strategy's own text describes its structures in the future tense, so that is not enough for implemented.

The law has been in force since 2019 and the Commission reports two trust service providers accredited in 2021 and registered today, so it is applied. The application is narrow: the State Audit Office found about 140 laws not aligned, a risk that institutions refuse electronic documents, and unconfirmed use of certificates. The 2025 amendments are rated separately.

The Assembly adopted the amendments on 15 July 2021 and the 2025 amending law cites them as part of the law in force. Commission reports on work permits describe the parent law, and no source shows these amendments' registration procedures in use, so nothing beyond adoption is shown.

The Commission states the portal has been upgraded and its offer widened, though in 2024 it said only a few new services had been added against a target of 135 or 139. Earlier reports describe the work as both ongoing and done, and whether the target was met is not stated. The State Audit Office's low-use findings concern the portal as a whole, so use of the upgrade is not shown.
The Commission reported that authorities continued to carry out activities under the strategy after its end date, having earlier called implementation fragmented.

The strategy ran out at the end of 2022 and its successor is the Cyber Security Strategy 2025-2028 (INT-MKD-0085). No source says it was repealed, so reversed is used by analogy with a replaced law because the scale has no value for expiry. The Government's later strategy says implementation was not fully achieved.
The Agency drafted the amendments in April 2022, and its 2026 report says the process of adopting them had still not started during 2025. No source reports adoption.

Parliament adopted the law on 27 June 2025 and the Commission confirms this, while noting it does not fully align with the EU regulation. Article 27 of the law says it will start to apply only from 1 June 2027, so it cannot be implemented at the freeze date. That provision is mapped in the data to the parent law INT-MKD-0030.

The wallet is a Reform Agenda step due by December 2027, and the October 2025 digital strategy still describes it in the future tense. The 2025 law provides the legal basis, but no source shows a wallet in operation.

The Commission confirms adoption on 27 June 2025 and publication on 4 July 2025, and treats the central document management system as still to be completed. A digital strategy row on preparing a new law is a plan row and does not contradict adoption. The link between the earlier Reform Agenda items and this law is inferred, as the entity note says.

The Commission's own reports repeatedly state that the country participates in and implements the agenda, and that it applies the Regional Roaming Agreement and benefits from the roaming-free zone. The State Audit Office also reports active participation in 2025. The Commission's word successfully is recorded as its view and is not assessed here.
The Agency's 2024 strategy calls for this law by early 2026, but its 2026 report says transposition had still not started during 2025. No source reports a law being adopted.

The package was adopted in 2019 and measures followed, including the portal and the coordination groups. The State Audit Office found about 140 laws still not aligned in March 2024, long after the deadline of 25 August 2020, so implementation is partial and the 2025 strategy repeats that finding.

The Commission reports a regional commitment to create the wallet by the end of 2027, and the Reform Agenda has the country taking part in the initiative. The Commission lists it among measures being launched, but no source shows it in operation.
Every source describes the data centre as a future step, the latest being the October 2025 digital strategy, and the Reform Agenda step begins with a feasibility study. No source shows it built.
Metamorphosis created the tool with the Agency, and the Agency took it over in 2024 and hosts it on its website. The rise in users is reported only by the Agency, which is not enough for in_practice.

This draft was published for consultation in December 2023 and no source reports its adoption under this title. A 2025-2028 strategy was adopted instead, but the sources do not say it is the outcome of this draft, so the last stated status is kept.
Phase 6 is a Reform Agenda step, and the Commission's November 2025 report still recommends upgrading to it. Phase 5 only went live in January 2025.

The Commission reports that approvals for 5G frequencies were granted and that 5G coverage keeps expanding, and the State Audit Office reports 96.99% population coverage. One frequency remained to be tendered in 2024, and that tender is rated separately as INT-MKD-0512.

The Commission describes the law as in place and says its citizenship conditions will need amending. The only description of how it works comes from the country presentation, so there is no specific evidence on its application.

The State Audit Office, reporting after its audit, describes eID as issued on registration and used to log in to the national portal and other portals. It also found that some portals require separate profiles and that high-level eID conditions did not raise use, so use is real but limited.
The office was set up in 2019, and the Commission says it publishes biannual reports on broadband development, which is specific evidence of it working.
The portal was launched and maintained by the ministry as the central catalogue before the outage reported from the start of 2025.

The country's presentation to the Commission in February 2025 describes the portal as in line with best practice, but the State Audit Office says it has not functioned since the beginning of 2025 because of procurement problems. The audit is given more weight because it is specific and independent. No later source says it was restored.
The register is a Reform Agenda step with a methodology due by the end of 2025. No source reports the register or the methodology as delivered.

The regulator published the tender in 2025 and received one compliant bid, but the decision was postponed and the deadline moved to 12 January 2026. No source gives the outcome, so the assignment is treated as work under way and not concluded.

The Commission says the 14 bylaws fall under later steps, some in December 2025 and some by December 2027, and the law sets six months for adopting them. No source up to the freeze date reports any as adopted.
The Commission reports adoption of the strategy and its action plan in December 2023. Later items only cite the strategy or restate plans, so no source shows measures carried out.

For North Macedonia this is an alignment aim only: the digital strategy says it will bring the country closer to the Digital Decade goals. The State Audit Office says full implementation is not yet possible without adequate infrastructure.

The State Audit Office records that the Government officially put ADA into use on this date.

The Commission reports in 2020 and 2023 that use of the system by institutions has increased. The Reform Agenda plans a further update, which is separate from the system already in use.
